comment: Files `check-mobile-platform.mjs` skips for both mobile platform rules (no bare `react-native/` subpath imports, no browser globals). Every entry names a file and carries a written reason; an entry naming a file that no longer exists fails the check. A `*.web.ts` filename convention was considered and rejected — it would silently exempt every future `.web.ts` anyone adds, which contradicts the mobile vault guide's statement that the WebCrypto Platform Variant below is the only place in libs/mobile allowed to hold a browser API.

exemptions.reason: Holds `require.resolve('react-native/jest/assetFileTransformer.js')`, the asset transformer React Native ships for Jest. There is no package-root export for it — the subpath IS the published interface for this one file — so the deep-import rule cannot be satisfied here without dropping the transformer. Exempted by name rather than by leaving `require.resolve` unparsed, so that the rule covers every call form and this single legitimate use is a recorded decision instead of a gap. Revisit when React Native publishes a root entry for the Jest transformer, or at the 0.80 upgrade when deep imports are removed and this breaks regardless.

The vault crypto Platform Variant (see CONTEXT.md): selected by the Vite `resolve.extensions` list in apps/mobile/vite.config.mts ('.web.ts' ahead of '.ts') because react-native-quick-crypto is a JSI module that does not bundle for react-native-web. It reaches `crypto.subtle` because WebCrypto is the web-target implementation of the same VaultCrypto interface the native path implements with react-native-quick-crypto — the two are wire-compatible by construction (see the file's own header comment), not a leak of browser APIs into shared mobile code.

The Vite web entry point for the mobile app's web target, mounting into `document.getElementById('root')` the way every Vite web entry does. It is not a variant of anything else in libs/mobile — apps/mobile/src/main.tsx is the React Native entry, and this file replaces it wholesale for the web build rather than standing in for one native module.
